Summer 2026 Kuali System Updates

During summer 2026 we will be implementing a comprehensive update to the Kuali curriculum management system. This essential update includes revisions to proposal forms and workflow processes to improve usability, reduce errors, and align with recent Faculty Senate Legislation that modified our course approval process.
Because this update affects both forms and workflow functionality, a temporary pause in all proposal submissions (courses, programs, and specializations) is necessary to ensure a smooth transition.

Proposals already in workflow will continue to move forward and may still be approved
Draft course, program, and specialization proposals can still be created and edited, but not submitted
On June 2, any proposals that have not advanced beyond the College Dean level will be returned to draft status. This step is necessary to reduce the number of proposals in workflow during system updates and minimize the risk of errors. Faculty will receive an email notification once the updates are complete and Kuali operations have resumed. At that point, they may resubmit any drafted proposals into the workflow.
During this update period, undergraduate curriculum items will be reviewed by the Special Summer Curriculum Committee, and in necessary cases, may be approved during the summer on behalf of the full Senate by the Faculty Senate Executive Committee per UM Appendix C, 4.3. Graduate curriculum items will be held for review by the Graduate Council at their first meeting of AY 2026–2027.

This temporary pause is an important step to ensure the system can better support our curriculum processes moving forward. This update also establishes a foundation for smaller, annual improvements in future years.
This update is a collaborative effort between the Office of the Registrar, Faculty Senate leadership, Kuali technicians, and URI IT staff who support integration between Kuali and eCampus.

University Registrar (Jack Humphrey)
Catalog Coordinator (Taylor Flynn)

1. System Updates in Kuali
We begin by working with Kuali technicians to update existing forms. This may include adding, removing, or modifying form elements (“gadgets”) to improve functionality and alignment with institutional needs.
2. Testing in Sandbox Environment
Updated forms are tested in the Kuali sandbox environment to ensure they function as intended before any live changes are made.
3. Integration Testing with eCampus
In collaboration with URI IT, we test how the updated Kuali workflows interact with eCampus to confirm system compatibility and data integrity.
4. Review and Refinement
Based on testing results, necessary adjustments are made to ensure the workflows and integrations function correctly and efficiently.
5. Production Deployment
Once testing is complete and the system is fully validated, Kuali technicians deploy the updates to the live production environment.
6. Return to Normal Operations
After deployment, standard Kuali operations resume with the updated system in place.

Faculty Senate Executive Committee

Through RI General Law §16-32-10, academic responsibility at URI is delegated to the President and the Faculty Senate. The Faculty Senate Executive Committee (FSEC) serves as the steering committee of the Senate. It represents the Senate in meetings with other University bodies and with the Provost, the President, and the URI Board of Trustees. Meetings of the FSEC are held weekly to coordinate the Senate’s business and its committees and address concerns within its jurisdiction.
For the description of the powers and duties of the Executive Committee, please see University Manual Appendix C: By-laws of the Faculty Senate, Section 4.1 – 4.9.

CASC Report #2024-2025-02October 10, 2024 Faculty Senate Meeting Context: URI awards graduating students academic honors according to the languagelocated at Section 8.22.40 (Academic Regulations) of the University Manual.

The two committees now agree the matter is ripe for introduction to the fullFaculty Senate.

To: URI Faculty Senate From: Peter Paton: Chair – Joint Classroom Steering Committee (JCSC) Members: Katie Babula, Keith Brown, Katherine Kittredge, Dean Libutti, Lenore Martin, Ann Morrissey, Janie Palm, David Porter, Ken Sisson, Leon Theim, Ryan Trimm, Jeff Ulricksen.
Date: 18 March 2022 Subject: Summary of JCSC allocations this year The JCSC has funds allocated annual for all General Assignment Classrooms on the Kingston campus.
The committee has allocated $400,000 annually for upgrades to Audio-visual technology and $300,000 for basic infrastructure within classrooms (e.g., chairs, tables, lecterns, blinds), so excludes big ticket items such as HVAC systems (which we are aware have issues in buildings but are beyond the committee).
The committee has a list of when all the AV technology in GAC classrooms has last been updated, and we try to upgrade equipment ~5 years.
Specific upgrades this year: Beaupre Projectors: Replace the outdated projectors in both Beaupre Lecture Halls with laser projectors $29,450 Ranger Hall Mac Minis Note- These new GACs will come online Fall 22- Summary: There are 11 GACs going online in Ranger hall as part of finishing the top 2 floors of the building.

On the project, classroom computers were listed as OFE (owner furnished equipment). $9,867 Computer upgrades: Computer upgrades for all the auditoria on campus along with other outdated machines in GAC classrooms $28,412.55 Active Learning Lite Classroom Quinn rms 214, 211, 209, Chafee 235, 244, 235, 251: Upgrade flat panel displays; Purchase 14 projectors as backup stock to replace projectors that cease to function: $69,834 Replace projection screens in Avedisian 170 and Ballentine 115. $10,448 Swan Hall Projector Replacement (16 Rooms) Summary: As we continue to work towards changing over all campus projectors to lasers (instead of lamps) swapping the entire buildings remaining lamp-based projectors out would be a bulk cost savings move.

It’s especially helpful in these spaces as newer projectors will always be brighter and all of Swan classrooms have windows which face towards the projected displays. $64,050 Lectern Furniture Update Summary: This project would allow for changing out the older solid wood lecterns in Chafee (2nd floor), Quinn (2nd floor), and Swan to the newer style lecterns that were put in place for the 21C project and in Bliss and Fascitelli Engineering building.
The metal lecterns allow for better airflow and

heat regulation of systems as well as offer ADA height adjustment to the primary instructor work surface. $116,050 AirMedia Wireless Presentation Device Updates Summary: We have various versions of the Crestron wireless presentation device deployed in classrooms based upon their installation year. Due to a Crestron program change, this means, from mobile devices, not all rooms are capable of fully mirroring device screens. This also results in there being 2 different Apps that instructors must know which one is the correct one to use with the device. Phasing out these older units eliminates this confusion and broadens system capability for faculty. This affects roughly 50 rooms. $51,396.40 Holdover Bill from FY 21: $11,683.40 Total spending to date: $391,191.13 Infrastructure fund: $300,000 annual allocation; We acquired 600 Learn2 chairs for 16 classrooms in Swan Hall (excluding Auditorium) using this year’s funds – those chairs were acquired for this academic year and the cost was $285,000. We also bought 16 accessible tables with adjustable height surfaces for the 16 classrooms in Swan Hall with remaining funds to accommodate students with disabilities for $15,000. Ken Sisson stated this was a problem for all classrooms on campus and there really needs to be greater efforts to provide infrastructure for students with disabilities.
